chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the prayer in the synagogues and the churches, so he said: 'Sprinkle (water) and pray.' He said, 'And I asked him about the houses of the Magians, so he said: 'Sprinkle (water) them and pray.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer in a synagogue, church, or Zoroastrian house according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of praying in the places of worship of the People of the Book and Zoroastrians, establishing that their structures are not inherently impure (najis). Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes merely sprinkling water (rushsh) to remove minor dust or impurities, reflecting the Shia principle of ease in worship and the distinct status of these communities compared to polytheists. This ruling underscores the theological view that their places of worship, while dedicated to other deities, retain a degree of purity suitable for Islamic prayer.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Salāt in the synagogue, and the churches, so heasws said: ‘Sprinkle (water) and pray Salāt’. He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about the house of the Magians, so heasws said: ‘Sprinkle (water) and pray (Salāt)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about performing Salah (prayer) in al-Biya‘ and churches. He (the Imam) said, ‘Sprinkle, then perform Salah (prayer).’ He (the narrator) has said that he then asked him (the Imam) about the houses of Zoroastrians. He (the Imam) said, ‘Sprinkle and perform Salah (prayer).”’
